features.user_visible_behavior: A death is charged at the tick Hypixel announces it rather than when a once-a-second tab poll notices the row has changed, and a wither-essence secret is credited to the player Hypixel names rather than to whoever clicked something in the last two seconds. verification_manual: NOT PERFORMABLE IN THIS REPOSITORY, and this list now says so rather than reading as a step somebody skipped. Loom's dev client has no valid Hypixel session (CLAUDE.md), so the steps below need a human to play a floor with a debug build and hand over the session file -- the same condition that keeps ingame-001 blocked. The feature is still `passing`: its verification_command covers the layer this repository can reach, exhaustively, and the layer it cannot is named here and in the notes instead of being implied to have been checked.
Play a real floor with the mod installed, telemetry on, and at least one death in the party.

In the session jsonl: every `death` should carry `source: CHAT`. A `source: TAB` means the chat line for that death did not arrive or did not match, and a `death_duplicate` next to it means both arrived and the dedup held. Zero `death` events in a run that had a death means the wiring does not fire at all.
In the same file: `chat_unparsed` lines are patterns that are wrong, quoted (redacted) so they can be corrected. Oruo's flavour prose is expected there and is not a defect.

For the secret path the open question is ORDERING: a `chat_secret` must arrive BEFORE the `secret` it attributes. Read `attributedBy` on each `secret` -- `chat` proves the ordering works. A `click` sitting next to a preceding `chat_secret` proves it does not, and **CHAT_WINDOW is NOT the fix for that**: `chatAttribution` runs a forward-only window from a line that has already landed, so there is nothing to widen toward. A late line needs the credit DEFERRED until the chat for that tick has been seen, which is a different change. Note also that a late `chat_secret` does not merely fail benignly - it can MIS-ATTRIBUTE the NEXT secret taken within CHAT_WINDOW ticks.

features.title: Identify a decoration's player by something other than list order
features.user_visible_behavior: Every party member's room is read off the map by *who* the decoration belongs to rather than by where it sits in the list, so the roster-skew blackout stops being necessary and no tick is ever spent with teammates unplaced.
verification_manual: CANNOT BE PERFORMED HERE. Loom's dev client cannot log in to Hypixel, and a decoration mapping needs at least two people on one floor. What follows is for whoever plays one.
Play a floor with at least two people in the party, ideally with a death in it, with the debug log on. Then read the session file.

Q1, the one that decides whether this feature can ever exist: do the decorations carry names? Nothing logs `MapDecoration.name()` today (that is `deconame-001`, which is one field in the `player_room` event). Until it does, this run cannot answer Q1 and answers only Q2 and Q3.

Q2 - does the order heuristic hold? Read `player_room`: `decoIndex` must be stable per player for as long as nobody dies or joins, and each player's `cell` must track a plausible path rather than jumping between rooms other players are in.

Q3 - does the blackout fire, and for how long? Read `roster_skew`. It fired ZERO times on the one committed run because that run was solo. Expect it around every death; `markers` and `alive` say which way the counts disagreed and the gap between the two events says for how many ticks teammates went unplaced.
features.blocked_reason: THE MECHANISM THIS ENTRY WAS WRITTEN AROUND DOES NOT EXIST, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The only concrete upgrade path the codebase named - the old comment at PartyTracker.kt:134-138, that NoammAddons reads the decoration's map key whose last character is a digit identifying the player slot, and that a MapItemSavedData accessor mixin would therefore remove the counting - is false in both halves. (1) `ClientboundMapItemDataPacket` carries `Optional<List<MapDecoration>>`, an UNKEYED list: no key is ever transmitted. `MapItemSavedData.addClientSideDecorations` clears the private map and re-keys every entry `"icon-" + i` from its own loop index - the string-concat bootstrap constants in that class are literally `icon-` and `frame-` - and the map is a LinkedHashMap, so an accessor mixin would return this client's own list order spelled as a string. Past nine decorations the "last character" is not even the whole index. (2) NoammAddons does not do what the comment said: `DungeonUtils.kt` reads `val index = key[key.lastIndex].digitToInt()` and uses it as an index into `livingTeammates` - the identical order heuristic, plus a defect this mod does not have, since the digit counts the local player's own marker while the list it indexes does not contain them. WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK IT: exactly one candidate channel survives the wire, `MapDecoration.name()` (`Optional<Component>`). Whether Hypixel populates it on a dungeon map cannot be answered from here. `deconame-001` adds the one debug field that would let a real party floor answer it. If the answer is no, this entry should be CLOSED rather than carried: there would be no client-side channel left, and party sync is not a fallback - it is forbidden by the design (README.md:9 "full per-player attribution with no party sync", SighteAddons.kt:24 "No packets are sent and nothing is automated").

features.notes:
THE TITLE THIS ENTRY CARRIED WAS 'Party sync instead of the decoration-order heuristic', AND THE MOD'S OWN DESIGN FORBIDS THAT. README.md:9 states the design achieves 'full per-player attribution with no party sync'; SighteAddons.kt:24 states 'No packets are sent and nothing is automated'. Party sync means sending something. Corrected in place, the way clear-001, schema-001 and chat-001 were, rather than left to be read as a sanctioned plan.

THE FAILURE MODE IT DESCRIBED WAS ALSO WRONG, AND THE CORRECTION IS NOW ASSERTED RATHER THAN PROSE. It said 'two players standing on one decoration are told apart'. Decorations are one per player; two players never share one. Two players in one ROOM produce two decorations a few pixels apart, and the order mapping may swap them - which is HARMLESS, because both pixels resolve to the same `Pos` cell. `PartyTrackerTest.two teammates in one room resolve to one cell whichever way round they are` pins that, and pins that a third teammate one room over is a genuinely different cell so the equality is not the grid being too coarse to tell rooms apart. The damaging failure is the COUNT MISMATCH that shifts assignments across DIFFERENT rooms - the map drops a dead player's marker 10-20 ticks before their tab row flips to DEAD - which `trustOrder` already guards by refusing to place teammates at all for those ticks. That is now asserted in both directions (a marker too few and a marker too many). The second half of 'and secrets are attributed per player' is out of scope and belongs to chat: SecretTracker.kt:15-22 is explicit that the action bar is a per-room number and the client only sees its own interactions, and chat-001 shipped the only real source Hypixel offers - a named finder, for wither essences only.

WHAT LANDED, AND WHY IT IS NOT THE FEATURE. The assignment was extracted out of `positions()` into a pure `PartyTracker.assign(roster, localSlot, isFrame) -> Assignment`. Behaviour is unchanged; the point is that `positions()` takes a MapItemSavedData and reads DungeonSession statics, so the heuristic had zero coverage and could not get any. This is the same seam SecretTracker.parseSecrets, PartyTracker.TAB, Pseudonym.row and ContributionTracker's TrackedRoom use, and it is a design decision, not a tidy-up: `ContributionTracker.tick` iterates `PartyTracker.positions(map)` and only ever creates a room some decoration resolved into, so how decorations map to players decides which rooms exist, get named, get cleared and get scored. Room discovery is inside this blast radius and was treated as first-class.

THE verification_command WAS VACUOUSLY GREEN AND IS NOW NOT. It named PartyTrackerTest, which already existed and already passed with cases covering only the tab regex and the living-class carry - nothing this entry touches, so it could not fail a session that did nothing. The command is deliberately UNCHANGED in text; what changed is that the class now contains 7 cases that exercise the assignment, and three mutation probes measure that it can fail (see evidence). Padding the command with more class names would have hidden that rather than fixed it.

NOT PAIRED, NO SCHEMA BUMP - VERIFIED MECHANICALLY, NOT TRUSTED. The decoration mapping changes the VALUES of playerTicks, playersInRoom, ownTicks, unattributed and enterTick and no key names. `build/keydiff.py` (re-created this session; chat-001 recorded its description but not the script) parses every addProperty key out of RunReport.build()/room() and RUN_KEYS/RUN_OPTIONAL/ROOM_KEYS/ROOM_OPTIONAL out of SighteAddonServerside/ingest.py: four empty sets, and all five of those keys present on both sides. RunReport.kt is untouched by this branch (`git diff 9cb71ee..HEAD -- src/main/kotlin/sighteaddons/RunReport.kt` empty) and SCHEMA is still 5. SighteAddonServerside was READ and NEVER WRITTEN.

features.notes:
README 'Known limits': the build compiles and the grid, timing and tab-parsing logic are unit tested, but calibration, decoration mapping, checkmark reading and core hashing have never run against real Hypixel data. The /sa screen is one step further down — its API use is pinned by the compiler and its record fold is unit tested, but no pixel of it has ever been on screen. Note also that the room database is version-coupled: core hashes are built from Block.toString() in a fixed order, so RoomDatabase.coreAt must be re-verified whenever Hypixel changes a room or Mojang changes that representation.

features.notes:
FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING clearpoints-001, recorded rather than fixed inline per CLAUDE.md. The receiver's agent/AGENT-PROMPT.md line 62 tells its analysis agent to look for '`unattributed` large relative to `roomsCleared` in `run_end`' — that gap is the documented diagnostic for a broken decoration->player mapping. The mod's run_end event (SighteAddons.kt:149) writes floor, roomsCleared, points, unnamed and newRecords, and NOT unattributed. So the receiver's runbook names a field that has never been in the log, and an analyst following it finds a hole rather than a signal. This is a one-field addition to a debug event: not a schema change, not paired (DebugLog is the mod's own JSONL and the receiver does not validate it), and no version bump. Worth doing deliberately anyway, because the alternative reading is that AGENT-PROMPT.md meant the per-room `unattributed` EVENT that award() emits, in which case the fix is on the receiver's side of the wire and is a different delegation — decide which before writing the line. Note also that the per-room `unattributed` event fires whenever the MIN_TICKS split was empty, including when the raw-presence fallback then credited somebody, so counting those events is NOT the same number as the run's unattributed rooms; whoever picks this up should say which of the two the analyst wants.

THAT AMBIGUITY NOW HAS A WORKED EXAMPLE FROM A REAL FLOOR, added 2026-08-14 by artifacts-001. On the M7 at docs/evidence/session-1786719912927/: exactly ONE `unattributed` event fired — Duncan, whose MIN_TICKS split was empty because it cleared six ticks after entry — and the raw-presence fallback then credited its whole 1.25 to p-cad01af7 anyway. So that run has ONE `unattributed` event and ZERO genuinely unattributed rooms, on a ten-room floor. The two numbers differ by one across the entire diagnostic range the receiver's analyst reads, which settles the question rather than merely illustrating it: WRITE THE RUN-LEVEL COUNT (ContributionTracker.unattributed(), the counted rooms), NOT THE EVENT COUNT. The event count would have told the analyst that 10% of the floor's decoration mapping was broken when in fact none of it was — exactly the false positive AGENT-PROMPT.md line 62 would act on. This does not change the feature's scope (still one field on one debug event, still not a schema change, still not paired) and it is not implemented; it removes the open question that was blocking a line from being written.

features.title: The mod cannot send a floor the receiver would reject
features.user_visible_behavior: A run played anywhere the sidebar names is uploaded rather than 400'd away, so no run is lost to a floor string the two sides spell differently.
verification_manual: Diff the value domain, not just the key set: every string DungeonSession.floor can hold against ingest.py's FLOOR pattern.
features.notes:
FOUND WHILE FIXING floorloss-001, 2026-08-15, and deliberately not fixed inline.

The receiver validates `floor` with FLOOR = re.compile(r"\?|E|[FM][1-7]") under fullmatch (ingest.py:93, used at ingest.py:225). The mod's own FLOOR regex is Regex("""The Catacombs \((\w+)\)""") and DungeonSession.floor's own KDoc has said since it was written that the values are "F7", "M7" or "Entrance". `Entrance` does not fullmatch that pattern - the receiver clearly expected `E`. A report carrying it is a 400, and TelemetryUpload never retries a 400, so the run is gone.

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT, measured rather than assumed: RunReport.write returns early on an empty room list, rooms are only ever added by ContributionTracker.tick, and that only runs once DungeonSession.update has calibrated against the Mort armor stand and the dungeon map - which exists only inside a floor instance, where the sidebar reads (F7)/(M7). The Catacombs Entrance is a separate Hypixel server, so arriving there is a JOIN and a reset. So no report with rooms in it can currently carry `Entrance`. floorloss-001 does not widen this: the floor is cleared on every JOIN either way.

WHAT THE WORK IS. Decide which side spells it, then make the two agree and TEST THE AGREEMENT rather than restating it. The cheap half is on this side (map `Entrance` -> `E` at the one point that files it, RunReport.reportedFloor) and needs no receiver change, no schema move and no pairing. The other half - teaching the validator the long spelling - is a receiver feature and would be paired. Prefer the first: `E` is already the shape the receiver's own regex was written for.

WORTH KNOWING EITHER WAY: build/keydiff.py compares KEY SETS and is clean here. It cannot see a value-domain mismatch, and this is the first one anybody has hit. That is a gap in the check, not a failure of it.

features.notes:
MEASURED, 2026-08-15, from three real M7 party runs on 0.10.0/0.11.0. 32 chat_unparsed events, and the sample is entirely PLAYER CHAT rather than unmatched Hypixel lines - e.g. '[p-bed304e3] p-3b5d9203 p-ae727fc2 p-347caa5c: I am p-3b5d9203 p-ae727fc2 p-347caa5c. I p-ad5d88b2 p-7c278c05'. Two defects in one line.

(1) The near-miss log records lines a human typed. Those can never match a dungeon pattern, so they are noise in the one place built to diagnose a pattern that stopped matching - chat-001's own recorded purpose for it.

(2) Pseudonym.row is applied to free chat text, so EVERY whitespace token becomes a pseudonym - 'I am ...' reads as three player ids. That is over-redaction rather than a leak, so it is not a privacy defect; but it makes the log unreadable for the diagnosis it exists for. Note this cuts both ways and the fix must not become an under-redaction: a player sentence can contain another player's name, which is exactly what Pseudonym exists to keep out of a permanent log.

SHAPE: skip lines that carry a chat prefix (a speaker before a colon) before logging a near miss, or log only lines that reached a pattern and failed. Not paired - DebugLog bodies are never parsed by the receiver (ingest.py validates the filename only).

features.title: The Explosive Shot crit, per Blessing of Power
features.user_visible_behavior: During the Maxor phase of M7, an Explosive Shot crit prints one line into your own chat: `Crit  12.0B  ·  power 8  ·  1.50B per power`. The announced damage is divided by the number of enemies hit, because the shot spreads it; that per-target figure is then divided by the floor's Blessing of Power (read from the tab list footer, plus 2.5 per Blessing of Time), which is what makes two crits from different runs comparable. `/sa` → chat → `crit readout` switches it off. Nothing is sent anywhere and nothing is typed into chat by the mod.
verification_manual: NOT PERFORMABLE IN THIS REPOSITORY. The dev client has no Hypixel session, so none of the steps below has been run; they need a human to play an M7 with a debug build. `./gradlew runClient` was used for one thing only — that the new tab-footer mixin accessor applies at class load rather than crashing the game on startup.
Enter M7. On Maxor's opening line the window opens; land an Explosive Shot crit and confirm exactly one line appears in your own chat and that NO party or /msg line is sent (ask a party member).
Check the number: the `B` figure should be the announced damage divided by the enemy count, divided by 1e9.

Open the tab list and read the blessings. `power N` on the line must equal the Blessing of Power numeral plus 2.5 per Blessing of Time. `power unknown` means the footer was not read at all — that is the accessor half failing and is the thing most likely to be wrong.
After Goldor speaks, land another crit and confirm nothing prints.

In the session jsonl: a `crit_unparsed` event is a crit line Hypixel sent that the pattern did not match, quoted verbatim. It is the ONLY thing that will confirm or correct the strings. Zero `crit_unparsed` AND zero readouts in a run with crits means the pattern matches nothing at all, or the window never opened.

features.title: Storm's cast countdown
features.user_visible_behavior: When Storm says `ENERGY HEED MY CALL!` or `THUNDER LET ME BE YOUR CATALYST!`, a large countdown appears under the crosshair: `Storm  6.9s`, blue above three seconds, yellow above one, red below. At zero it becomes `SHOOT NOW` in red for one second and then disappears. `/sa` -> hud -> `storm timer` switches it off; the two rows under it step the countdown and the SHOOT NOW window a tick at a time (shift-click steps back), because 138 and 20 are inherited numbers nobody here can derive. Nothing is sent anywhere and nothing is typed into chat by the mod.
verification_manual: NOT PERFORMABLE IN THIS REPOSITORY. The dev client has no Hypixel session and no dungeon, so none of the steps below has been run; they need a human to play an M7 with a debug build. Unlike critcalc-001 this feature adds no mixin and no HudElementRegistry registration, so there was nothing for `./gradlew runClient` to prove and it was not run.
Enter M7 and reach Storm. On either of his two lines the countdown must appear under the crosshair, and NO party or /msg line may be sent (ask a party member).
Watch it change colour: blue, then yellow with three seconds left, then red with one.
At zero it must read SHOOT NOW in red for one second and then vanish. Whether that is the right MOMENT is exactly what nobody knows - see the notes.

Open /sa -> hud. `storm countdown` and `storm shoot window` must show `138 ticks - 6.90s` and `20 ticks - 1.00s`; clicking steps +1 tick, shift-clicking -1, and both must survive a game restart (they are written to config.json).

In the session jsonl, TWO events settle this and they mean different things. `storm_start` is the wiring working: the line arrived, matched, and started a clock. `storm_unparsed` quotes verbatim a `[BOSS] Storm:` line that was NOT one of the two triggers. FAILURE SIGNALS: storm_unparsed present and storm_start absent means the two strings are wrong and the event says what Storm actually says. BOTH absent in a run where Storm spoke means the line never reached SighteAddons.onChat at all - a delivery or stripping fault, not a wording one - and no amount of correcting the strings would fix it.
